name: International Protection (UNHCR Mandate Refugee Status Determination)

requirements.blocker_text: Must establish a well-founded fear of persecution in the country of origin to a UNHCR-conducted mandate refugee status determination interview.

sources.title: UNHCR Northern and Eastern Caribbean -- Apply for asylum through UNHCR: UNHCR (via its Panama office) conducts mandate refugee status determination at the request of the government for Antigua and Barbuda (along with Anguilla, Barbados, and other listed territories/states), since no domestic asylum system exists; interview process, right to an interpreter and legal representation, appeal within 30 days of a negative decision

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Antigua and Barbuda's initial build. Antigua and Barbuda has NO domestic asylum/refugee-status-determination law or agency -- UNHCR itself conducts mandate refugee status determination for claimants physically present in the country, at the government's request, via its Panama regional office, rather than any Antiguan and Barbudan ministry or the Immigration Department. Modelled as DRAFT rather than published: (a) the source is tier-2 (UNHCR, intergovernmental) rather than tier-1 government, since no Antiguan and Barbudan government page describing this process was found; (b) it is unclear from this pass what legal status (if any) a recognised mandate refugee is granted locally by the Antigua and Barbuda government once UNHCR determination is positive -- e.g. whether local work/study rights, a residence permit, or a path to local integration follows recognition, or whether the practical outcome is solely third-country resettlement referral. work_rights, study_rights, and family_can_join are conservatively modelled as none/false pending that gap being closed, since no local legal status was confirmed. Whether Antigua and Barbuda is a party to the 1951 Refugee Convention/1967 Protocol was not confirmed in this pass either -- flagged as a further open question, not assumed either way.
